title: Ensemble burst calibration log - camila
content: Purpose: quick scratchpad for a weird class of burst patterns where multiple small bursts overlap ("phase-locked") and cause surprising p99 spikes. Goal: find a small set of adaptive knobs (coalescing window, preemptive routing thresholds, model fanout) that reduce p99 by >= 30% without hurting p50 and throughput.
experiments: EXP-A: baseline - single model (gptq-6b-fused), A100-1x, no coalescing, standard routing. Arrival: compound Poisson: baseline 50 qps with occasional microbursts: 10 bursts/min, each burst = Poisson(λ=30) arrivals over 200ms. Warm cache. Result: p50=18ms, p95=54ms, p99=340ms, p999=920ms. Throughput saturated at 110 qps sustained during bursts (queueing). Notes: long tail aligns with simultaneous KV cache misses when two bursts hit same shard.

EXP-B: ensemble-fanout - route 30% of requests to small low-latency model (tiny-1.3b) when request size < 64 tokens. Same hardware, no coalescing. Result: p50=16ms, p95=48ms, p99=220ms, p999=610ms. Throughput similar. Observation: partial offload reduces tails but correctness drift in a tiny subset (~0.8% responses deviate on hallucination score). TODO: add eval set check for fallback correctness.

EXP-C: coalescing sweep - introduce adaptive coalesce window with min=0ms, max=12ms, probe every 30s. Arrival same as A. Result at stable config (window=6ms): p50=17ms, p95=45ms, p99=150ms, p999=400ms. Throughput increased under burst (peaked 150 qps) because batching amortization. BUT client-visible jitter spike at 6ms boundary for some single-token requests (client deadline 50ms). Action: add route-level SLAs to avoid coalescing for deadlines < 80ms.

EXP-D: kv-cache priming - synthetic preheat: when model warmup detected, prefetch top-10 tokens for popular prefixes (from recent 1h window). Combined with coalescing window=8ms and ensemble-fanout. Result: p50=15ms, p95=43ms, p99=112ms, p999=320ms. Cache hit rate jumped from 73% -> 92% within first 2 minutes of a burst. Note: prefetch increases memory footprint on shards; need limit per-host.

EXP-E: jitter injection / phase alignment - artificially offset multiple traffic streams by N ms to simulate 'phase-lock'. Observed: when offsets aligned within +/-2ms, p99 jumps 2.5x relative to random offsets. Hypothesis: scheduling quantization on the GPU side + request bundling threshold creates synchronized flush points. Follow-up: add random jitter (1-3ms) at ingress to de-synchronize. Quick test: ingress jitter 1.5ms reduced p99 by ~28% for aligned case.

EXP-F: FFT on latency time-series - ran short-window FFT on 1s-resolution p99 series during 20 minute run. Found dominant frequency ~4 Hz during bad bursts (period ~250ms). Interpretation: burst substructure repeating at ~250ms. Might correspond to batching tick + queue draining across 4 p50-buckets. Suggest altering batching tick phase per worker.

EXP-G: preemptive-routing policy - if queue length > Qthresh (20) and tail probability > .02 in last 30s, route to small model or enqueue with longer coalesce window. Result: p99 reduced another ~12% but 0.3% of requests saw degraded answer quality. Need to tie this to automatic retraining of the guardrail evaluator.

Raw CSV sample (latency histogram snapshot at t=2026-02-24T14:12:00Z):

0-10,12400
10-30,3100
30-100,420

Configuration notes: hardware: A100-80GB vGPU x1; model variants: gptq-6b-fused (fp16 kv), tiny-1.3b (int8); batching: continuous-batcher with max_batch_tokens=4096; kv cache TTL=30m; ingress jitter disabled by default (enable for next run).

Quick conclusions: 1) small random ingress jitter (1-3ms) is a very cheap, high-impact mitigation for phase-locked bursts. 2) adaptive coalescing with an upper bound ~8ms gives the best trade for our workload—amortizes tokens without breaking short-deadline requests when route-level guards exist. 3) ensemble offload reduces tails but needs automatic correctness monitoring to avoid silent quality regressions. 4) KV prefetching is strong but requires host memory guardrails.
Open questions / next steps: - Can we implement a low-overhead per-route deadline tag to bypass coalescing automatically? (Riley)
- Run scaled test on Dedicated cluster (4 hosts) to validate no cross-host synchronization artifacts (Noah)
- Add eval harness that samples 1% of offloaded responses for semantic diff against primary model; log to anomaly detector (Aisha)
- Explore staggering batching tick offsets per worker (random start offset 0-12ms) to break harmonic frequency.
notes: Scratch: don't merge into perf/batching branch yet. These are messy logs; will extract into a cleaned RFC once experiments repeated on dedicated capacity. Kept some raw timestamps and CSV for reproducibility. If we standardize an "ensemble-safety" evaluator, it should live under perf/evals/ensemble-safety and be runnable in CI. Also note: client SDK should expose soft_deadline to allow route-level bypassing of coalescing.
final_quick_action_items: Enable ingress jitter 1.5ms on staging for 48h
Create JIRA ticket for per-route soft_deadline header
Prototype deterministic evaluator for tiny-model offloads (1% sample)
Limit KV prefetch memory per host to 2GB default
